title: Finite etale free generators lift epimorphisms onto constructible sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, i.e. a quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, with constant sheaves of rings $A_X$, $A_{U}$ on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For every epimorphism $p:M\twoheadrightarrow C$ of sheaves of $A$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], with $C$ constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], there are finitely many separated etale finite-type morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $u_i:U_i\to X$ and a morphism $e:\bigoplus_i (u_i)_!A_{U_i}\to M$ such that $p\circ e$ is an epimorphism. Here $(u_i)_!$ is etale extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], and the finite direct sum may be combined into one over a finite disjoint union.

source.place: Tag 095N (Section 59.74 = Tag 095M, Lemma etale-cohomology-lemma-category-constructible-modules, line 12412): its proof applied to the composite of a possibly infinite surjection $\bigoplus_{i\in I}j_{U_i!}\underline{\Lambda}_{U_i}\to M$ (Modules on Sites, lemma module-filtered-colimit-constructibles) with $p$, followed by the constructible-topology compactness argument selecting a finite $I'\subset I$; affine $U_i$ etale over Noetherian $X$ are separated and of finite type over $X$.

proof.text: Write G_U=(u_U)_!A_U for each affine etale object U over X. These form a separating family by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-rank-one-separating], in the site and Hom-set universe specified there. Let I be the set of pairs (U,h:G_U\to M). The coproduct exists by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](2). Let q be the map whose summand (U,h) is h. If a q=b q, precomposition with every coprojection gives a h=b h for every U,h; the separating-family statement gives a=b. Thus q is epic. Each u_U is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. Since X is Noetherian, it is locally Noetherian and hence quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]; thus X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes each affine-source etale map quasi-compact and of finite presentation. In particular it is locally of finite type, so is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Lemma 093B(2), lemma-module-quotient-direct-sum, in Situation 0937; affine separating-family coproduct argument of 03EW(3).

proof.text: For each finite subset J\subset I, let G_J=\bigoplus_{i\in J}(u_i)_!A_{U_i} and let g_J:G_J\to C be the composite of the inclusion into the coproduct, q, and p. Recall from Step 1 that X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and each U_i is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Each summand is constructible by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-free-sheaf-constructible], and finite sums are constructible by the Serre closure theorem [thm-constructible-serre]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-surjectivity-locus] applies to g_J and shows that its geometric-stalk failure locus T_J={x\in X\mid (g_J)_{\bar x} is not surjective} is constructible.

source.place: Tag 095N, lemma-category-constructible-modules, proof of the finite surjection (lines 12432--12459), with Tag 095E for constructible cokernels

proof.text: Fix a geometric point \bar x. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], the forgetful functor to abelian sheaves is faithful and exact and carries the coproduct defining q to the coproduct of the underlying abelian sheaves; hence the underlying maps of q and p are epic. The stalk maps q_{\bar x} and p_{\bar x} are surjective because geometric stalks are exact [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact]. Moreover [lem-kun-stalks-commute-colimits] identifies the stalk of the coproduct with the coproduct of the stalks, so every element has finite support. The target stalk C_{\bar x} is a finitely generated A-module by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-finite-stalks]. Choose finitely many target generators and lifts first through p_{\bar x}, then through q_{\bar x}; all these lifts lie in (G_J)_{\bar x} for one finite J. Hence x\notin T_J, and the intersection of all T_J (over finite J\subset I) is empty.

source.place: Tag 095N, proof of lemma-category-constructible-modules, finite-type stalk and finite-support argument at lines 12455--12460

proof.text: Since X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (Step 1), its underlying space is spectral by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-finite-intersection] to the family (T_J): there are finite subsets J_1,\ldots,J_r of I whose failure loci have empty intersection. Let J_0=J_1\cup\cdots\cup J_r. Since enlarging J can only add generators, T_{J_0}\subseteq\bigcap_kT_{J_k}=\emptyset.

source.place: Tag 095N, final constructible-topology compactness argument, lines 12455--12466

proof.text: For every x\in X, with \bar x the geometric point at an algebraic closure of \kappa(x) used in Step 2, x\notin T_{J_0}, so (g_{J_0})_{\bar x} is surjective. Let K=coker(g_{J_0}) in the module-sheaf category. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], its underlying abelian sheaf is the cokernel of the underlying map, and exactness of geometric stalks identifies K_{\bar x} with the cokernel of the surjective stalk map, so every geometric stalk of K is zero. For each scheme point s use the geometric point at the algebraic closure of \kappa(s), as specified in the blueprint update of [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. Apply that conservative statement to the map from the underlying abelian sheaf of K to zero. Its stalk maps are isomorphisms, so that sheaf is zero; faithfulness of the forgetful functor then gives K=0. The abelian-category criterion epi iff zero cokernel makes g_{J_0} an epimorphism.

source.place: Tag 095N, finite-surjection conclusion after the constructible-topology argument

proof.text: Let e:G_{J_0}\to M be the finite-coproduct inclusion followed by q; then p e=g_{J_0} is epic. Form U=\coprod_{i\in J_0}U_i and u:U\to X using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]; its components are clopen and cover U. Etaleness, separatedness and finite type follow componentwise: there are no cross-component diagonal terms, and the finite union of finite affine covers over any affine open of X is finite. To check u_!A_U=\bigoplus_i(u_i)_!A_{U_i}, use the sheafified sum-over-lifts construction [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension]. A lift s:V\to U partitions V into the clopen pieces V_i=s^{-1}(U_i). The coefficient section on V is exactly the tuple of its restrictions to these pieces, by the sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. On this covering, the summand indexed by s belongs to the corresponding (u_i)_! summand; conversely the summands for lifts V\to U_i map to those for V\to U. These maps are inverse after restriction to the V_i, hence after sheafification. Sheafification of the finite presheaf sum is the sheaf coproduct by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](2). This proves the asserted identification, including the empty union, whose extension is zero.

proof_origin.place: Tag 095N, proof of the finite surjection, using Modules on Sites Lemma 093B(2) in Situation 0937 for the initial free epimorphism.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q130-c2949fa92 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. It has 6 steps and no new nodes; the former helper was folded into Step 1. I checked it against Stacks 095N (etale-cohomology.tex lines 12412-12466) and 093B(2) (sites-modules.tex line 5203, Situation 0937). The item applies the 095N argument to p∘q, so the epimorphism M->C can be arbitrary, which is what the parent lem-trf-constructible-free-etale-resolution needs. The statement is unchanged and not weakened. Edge cases checked: X empty, C=0, I empty (forces M=0), M of infinite rank, p an isomorphism. The only near-duplicate candidate, new-constructible-affine-free-presentation-general, is a finite presentation of F itself and not this lift through an arbitrary epimorphism. Each cited statement's hypotheses hold where it is used: the separating family needs no hypotheses; colimits-forgetful (1)-(3); affine-source separated; qcqs permanence (1); free-sheaf-constructible and surjectivity-locus need X qcqs, U affine and A finite; Serre closure (finite sums are extensions); stalks commute with colimits; constructible stalks are finite; spectral space and finite intersection; the conservative lemma in its blueprint_update form at algebraic-closure points. Step 6's disjoint-union identification is accepted. I repaired two faults (fix file written). (C1) 'Noetherian ⇒ quasi-separated' was used without a citation in Step 1 and implicitly in Steps 2 and 4: Step 1 now cites the existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated (added to uses and proof_deps), and Steps 2 and 4 now say that X and the affine U_i are qcqs. Step 5 claimed surjectivity at every geometric point, which is more than Step 4 gives; it now claims it only at the algebraic-closure point of each x. I accept the declared tool uses: generic infrastructure that unit sk-i-curve-zero does not replace. No SGA is cited.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
